title: Squashing, Bending, Twisting, Stretching
seo_title: Year 2 Science: Changing the Shape of Materials Worksheets (Squash, Bend, Twist, Stretch)
standard_text: Find out how the shapes of solid objects made from some materials can be changed by squashing, bending, twisting and stretching.
meta_desc: Free Year 2 science worksheets on changing the shape of materials: squashing, bending, twisting and stretching, which materials spring back and an elastic band test. 100 questions with answers.
key_sub: Some materials spring back; others keep their new shape.
body_html:
How to think about it

Pushes and pulls can change an object's shape.

  • Squash, bend, twist and stretch.
  • Soft or bendy materials change shape easily; hard ones do not.
  • Some spring back; some stay in their new shape.
Example

Wringing out a wet cloth?

Ends turn opposite ways

Answer: twisting

Example

Does clay spring back after squashing?

It keeps its new shape

Answer: No

Common mistakes

  • Thinking all materials can be stretched.
  • Thinking squashed things always spring back.
  • Thinking twisting and bending are the same.

faq.q: How can we change the shape of an object?
faq.a: By squashing, bending, twisting or stretching it with a push or a pull.
Soft or bendy materials such as sponge, modelling clay, elastic bands and pipe cleaners. Hard materials such as brick, stone and glass do not.

faq.q: Do things go back to their old shape?
faq.a: Some do, like a sponge or an elastic band. Others, like modelling clay or crushed foil, stay in their new shape.
